findings.title: Architect's 'named-mode-explore emit-timing genre' citation goes stale under the timing delta
findings.recommendation: The live orbit-architect baseline says architect emits at conversation boundaries '(the named-mode-explore emit-timing genre)' — but the delta reclassifies named-mode explore to the begin+boundary genre while architect's bullet in the delta'd timing requirement stays boundary-only. Post-archive the baselines contradict: an implementer following the genre citation could give architect a begin emit D3 deliberately does not grant. Exactly the un-delta'd-enumeration class (not CRITICAL: architect's operative SHALLs remain unambiguous). Add a one-line MODIFIED delta to orbit-architect's 'Architect run-summary emit' requirement rewording the parenthetical (e.g. 'the conversation-boundary timing per orbit-run-summary-emit; architect fires no begin emit — the begin+boundary genre is explore's').

findings.title: Two shape points inside the shared workstream entry are still implementer-divergent
findings.recommendation: (a) 'a CHANGE entry embeds the same per-change status payload --change --json emits' — the enumerated shape {name, kind, stage?, strip, position, last, next, gates?} reads closed, so it is undefined whether the payload's fields SPREAD into the entry or NEST under a key; two implementers produce incompatible JSON. (b) `strip` has no declared JSON type — the requirement's 'computed chips ride on its strip field' plus the design's layout-control risk line point at a structured chip array, but nothing forbids a pre-rendered string. Pin both in the JSON-output requirement: name the embedding (e.g. the payload nests under a `status` key) and declare strip's type (e.g. an ordered array of {phase, glyph, detail?} chips from the closed glyph mapping, with the text render derived from it). Ripple tasks 2.3/5.1.

findings.title: No explicit read-only guarantee on the orientation surface
findings.recommendation: engine-gates' slice has 'No new files written by state computation'; orientation's collection has only the design-level 'pure recompute, no caching' note — the spec's data-source limits constrain reads, not writes. Add one clause ('the surface creates and modifies no files') to the no-live-inference scenario or fault-isolation clause (c), making task 5.1's fs-access assertion two-sided.
